metadata.case_name: CHAN YU CHAU v. FONG ON CONSTRUCTION & ENGINEERING CO. LTD.

injuries.description: amputation of the right thumb at the proximal phalangeal joint
source: he was found to have sustained amputation of the right thumb at the proximal phalangeal joint
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation at or near base of right thumb

injuries.description: amputation of the right index finger at the metacarpo phalangeal joint
source: amputation of the right index finger at the metacarpo phalangeal joint
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation of other single finger

injuries.description: amputation of the right middle finger at the proximal phalangeal joint
source: and amputation of the right middle finger at the proximal phalangeal joint
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation of other single finger

manifestations.description: his right hand has only about 1/3 of the power grip of the left hand
He cannot make a pincer grip for fine finger manipulation of an object with his right hand
his ability in hammering and nailing is affected as he cannot hold a hammer tightly during hammering
he has to raise his forearm to place the stumps at an appropriate angle of approach
He can no longer use chopsticks with his right hand
the injuries seriously affect his ability to write
He complains of not being able to tie his shoelaces
embarrassment when people look at his right hand when he walks in the street
it affects his mood leading him to lose his temper more easily

treatments_received: emergency operation (attempt to restore severed digits)
operation on 1998-03-17 to remove the amputated digits

losses.description: Loss of right thumb, index and middle fingers resulting in severely reduced power grip (about 1/3 of left), inability to make a pincer grip and impairment of manual tasks such as hammering and nailing

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Cannot use chopsticks with right hand; cannot tie shoelaces; ability to write seriously affected
Embarrassment when people look at his right hand when he walks in the street
Unable to continue as a formwork 'Master'; limited to lower paid formworker work and unable to take on contracts himself
